question: In the seventeenth century, Peter Mundy, a foreign traveller from __________ visited India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**England**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Peter Mundy was an English traveller who visited India during the early 17th century.
 
• He is known for his detailed accounts of his travels in India and other parts of Asia.
 
• Mundy's observations provide valuable insights into the social, economic, and cultural conditions of India during the Mughal period.
 
• His travels were part of the broader movement of English merchants and explorers seeking to establish trade relations in the East.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **17th Century Context:**

 
 
• The 17th century was a period of significant exploration and trade expansion by European powers in Asia.
 
• England, under the East India Company, was actively seeking to establish and expand its trade networks in India.
 
 
 
• **East India Company:**
 
 
• The East India Company was founded in 1600 to exploit trade with East and Southeast Asia and India.
 
• It played a crucial role in the establishment of British colonial rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Empire:**
 
 
• During Peter Mundy’s visits, India was under the rule of the Mughal Empire, which was one of the largest and richest empires of the time.
 
• The Mughal Empire was known for its administrative efficiency, military prowess, and architectural achievements.
 
 
 
• **Travel Literature:**
 
 
• Peter Mundy's writings are part of a larger genre of travel literature that provides historical insights into the regions visited by European explorers and traders.
 
• These writings are valuable historical documents that help historians understand the dynamics of the period.
